questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wished to explore a country that was very different from mine both in terms of culture, geography, and history, and Australia fulfilled each of these criterias.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit confusing finding the relevant information for my stay upon arrival, as we had received a fair amount of e-mails regarding different aspects of student life. However, through the help of fellow exchange students, I was able to locate the needed information regarding the stay. I also got some help from the student dorm where I stayed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had received a lot of information through e-mails, and some orientation briefings upon arrival. Most of it were practical information, but there was also a lot of information regarding social events to meet other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student accommodation dormitories

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We didn't receive much regarding meal plans, but there were decent shared cooking facilities available. However, we had to purchase all kitchen equipment and utensils ourselves

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That you have to either bring or purchase items for use in kitchens, rooms, and other facilities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit time consuming and extensive, but otherwise relatively fine. Our student coordinator replied quickly, and most steps during the process were pretty easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student coordinator both in Denmark and Australia.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all the classes that I had applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and get in touch with the coordinator if you experience any issues.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses varied a bit, with some being quite difficult and challenging academically, but still really interesting. There was also quite a bit of difference regarding the level of academic theories and scholars used for the different courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In many ways, I found a lot of similarities between the teaching styles of my host institution and UCPH, as I primarily have seminar/tutorial style classes in both.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Rethinking Poverty, Indigenous Rights - Global Issues, Cultures of Violence, and Digital Media and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All courses

questions.answer: Student visa

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than anticipated

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many different activities available for students, ranging from sports clubs to different societies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The bouldering society

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All of the national parks and beaches around the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to adjust, as the dorm was located close to all amenities, the campus, and not far from the beautiful city center.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found that I mostly socialized with other exchange students and foreign students, but this was also due to the fact that many of my classes consisted mostly of non-Australian students. I did however, find that Australian students were very nice and sociable.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe that stores close quite early compared to at home. Australia also have many strange rules and regulations that can be quite difficult to understand sometimes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed lifestyle.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be patient, embrace the unknown, and just enjoy yourself and your new home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it is important to familiarize yourself beforehand with what types of exams/assignments that are required for each unit of study that you choose.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Embracing a completely different culture and world, with all of its positives and negatives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being far away from friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If anyone is wondering whether they should go on exchange - just do it! It is the most amazing, rewarding, and challenging thing that a student can do, and it will change your life. :-)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
